headline: Peptide ADMET evidence and multimodal prediction meet auditable evaluation standards
label: Peptide Admet Resources And Evaluation
summary: Poor permeability and limited in vivo stability still decide whether peptide candidates reach the clinic, driving new ADMET resources and models.
synthesis: The dominant thread is peptide pharmacology. ADMETatlas aggregates peptide ADMET evidence in an online database, motivated by permeability and in vivo stability as clinical gatekeepers. Pepti-DrugPhAI extends this direction with a multimodal model that processes SMILES and amino acid sequences together to predict peptide ADMET properties and toxicity. What is new is pairing peptide-specific evidence and multimodal prediction with explicit evaluation. Adjacent items address evaluation rigor more broadly: a perspective proposes an L0-L5 cold-start framework and leakage checklist for DDI and DTI models, and a PBPK study shows that dose-driven exposure and safety limits reorder PARP1 generated molecules. These works share a concern that performance claims must be auditable and exposure-aware before candidates are ranked, constraining how results from such tools can be compared.
